The present continuous tense (also called the present progressive tense) is a tense commonly used in English. This is how we form and use this tense.

Form: subject + be + verb -ing
Example:
He is trying to maintain his ego.

Use:
  1. We use the present continuous to talk about actions or situations which are in progress at the moment of speaking.
    • He is doing a fantastic job at the party.
    • She's really enjoying her new role.
    • I'm just being protective of you.
    • He is flirting with her.

  2. We use the present continuous to talk about actions or situations which are in progress around the present time, but not necessarily at the moment of speaking.
    • I'm getting to meet a lot of people at the party.
    • Maria is modelling some of their new clothes.

When speaking a foreign language, especially English, it is important that you acquire a set of conversation strategies which will help you deal with the spontaneity of spoken English. A very important strategy you need to master is changing topics in a conversation. Here are a few expressions you can use to change the subject of a conversation.

• But ... + question.
  • Funny you should say that. Did I ever tell you about the time + clause?
  • Speaking of + noun, + new topic.
  • Oh, while you're at it, + new topic.
  • Oh, + new topic

Amy: Hey, are you enjoying the party?
Brian: Yes, but ... is Maria coming?

Amy: There's a lot of good food here.
Brian: Speaking of food, did I tell you about the new Japanese restaurant downtown?
Oh, check it out! Mark is chatting with the secretary.

These are words you use to describe a social event.
a general feeling you get from a place
Example: The party had a good vibe.
a high social position that makes other people respect or admire you
Example: The events will bring an international status to Holly's clothing line.
Example: This is part of showbiz, Peter.
to have the opportunity to interact with people
Example: I get to meet many beautiful women here.
a formal public event with special traditions, actions, or words
Example: This is a very well-planned ceremony.
You are going to play a game with your partner.
Before you start, write 4-5 different topics for a conversation on cards. Do the same for changing the topic expressions.
You are going to start by telling a story about something that happened to you recently.
Your partner will pick a “conversation card” and a “changing the topic card”. He or she will change the topic of the conversation.
Do this until you run out of cards.
You can also use vocabulary you learned from the lesson to review words. Then, before changing topics, you also need to pick a vocabulary card and raise a new topic related to that word.
